summary: First testing iteration for Fabric Catalog system. Backend: 31/34 pytest cases pass (91%). Frontend: login, dashboard, all sidebar nav, charts, dark mode, logout, and scanner autofocus work. Found 3 real backend bugs: (a) POST /api/scans returns 500 due to leftover Mongo ObjectId _id in response body (this also breaks the frontend Scanner page), (b) POST /api/auth/reset-password returns 500 due to naive vs tz-aware datetime comparison on expires_at, (c) brute-force lockout is ineffective behind the k8s ingress because identifier uses request.client.host (internal pod IP that varies across replicas). Also: post-login navigates to '/' instead of '/dashboard' (UX nit; content still renders).

critical.issue: 500 - leftover Mongo ObjectId _id in response. After db.scan_history.insert_one(doc), the dict is mutated with _id (ObjectId). Endpoint returns {'catalog': doc_to_json(cat), 'scan': doc} but does NOT pop _id from `doc`, so FastAPI's jsonable_encoder fails with TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable. Fix: doc['id'] = str(doc.pop('_id')) before return, OR return doc_to_json(doc).

500 - TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes at server.py:338. password_reset_tokens.expires_at is stored as a tz-aware datetime via insert_one (kept as native datetime, not ISO string), but motor returns it back as a NAIVE datetime. Comparison `rec['expires_at'] < now()` where now() is tz-aware raises. Fix: store as ISO string (like other dates) and parse on read, OR ensure tz-awareness on comparison (e.g. expires_at = expires_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)).

Lockout ineffective behind load balancer. identifier = `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"` resolves to k8s internal pod IPs (e.g. 10.219.11.197, 10.219.0.93) that load-balance per request, so each replica only sees ~1-2 attempts and never reaches 5. Confirmed reproducible: 7 sequential wrong-password POSTs through the public URL all returned 401, login_attempts collection had two docs split across pod IPs. Fix: key on email only (or honor X-Forwarded-For with a configured trust list).

minor.issue: Inconsistent return shapes: create_category/supplier/catalog manually pop _id and set id, while /scans forgets. Recommend wrapping with doc_to_json() consistently.
Cookies are set httpOnly + samesite=lax with `secure=False`. Should be secure=True over HTTPS in production for cookie hardening (low risk in preview).

ui_bugs.issue: After successful login frontend navigates to '/' instead of '/dashboard' (Protected route renders Dashboard at root, so functionally OK but URL is misleading; broke our wait_for_url('**/dashboard**')).
Submitting a valid barcode triggers POST /api/scans which returns 500 (see backend critical bug #1), so the scanner UI shows no catalog result and console logs a 500.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend scanner submission fails end-to-end due to backend /api/scans 500

action_items: Fix POST /api/scans to strip Mongo _id before returning (e.g. return {'catalog': doc_to_json(cat), 'scan': doc_to_json(doc)}).
Fix POST /api/auth/reset-password datetime comparison (store expires_at as ISO string OR coerce to UTC-aware on read).
Replace IP-based brute-force identifier with email-only key (or trust X-Forwarded-For) so lockout works behind k8s ingress.
Optional: redirect post-login navigate('/dashboard') instead of navigate('/') for clearer UX.
Optional: harden cookies to secure=True when running over HTTPS.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 932 lines - acceptable for an MVP but should be split (auth, catalogs, reports, etc.) once it grows further.
doc_to_json() helper is good but inconsistently applied (e.g. /scans return path).
expires_at stored as native datetime (line 327) while every other timestamp uses iso(now()) - inconsistent and is the direct cause of the reset-password 500.

Brute force lockout per IP+email is the standard pattern but only works if request.client.host is the *real* client; behind k8s ingress this is the previous-hop IP and load-balances across replicas. Configure --forwarded-allow-ips / X-Forwarded-For trust or drop the IP component.
audit() uses request.client.host with no proxy handling - audit IPs will likewise show internal pod IPs.

Catalog create_at/updated_at stored as ISO strings everywhere - the regression date filters in dashboard/charts depend on lexicographic ISO ordering which works (good) but cannot be indexed for range performance easily.
Reports endpoints accept any authenticated user (including staff). If business rule requires admin/manager only, add require_role.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (login, dashboard, charts, all nav, scanner autofocus, dark mode, logout all work; scan submission fails due to backend bug)

rca_of_the_issue: 1) /api/scans 500: pymongo insert_one mutates the inserted dict in-place adding ObjectId _id; the endpoint returns that dict directly and FastAPI's jsonable_encoder can't serialize ObjectId. 2) reset-password 500: expires_at stored as datetime (not ISO string), motor returns naive datetime on read, server compares with tz-aware now() -> TypeError. 3) Brute force lockout fail: behind k8s ingress, request.client.host = internal load-balancer pod IP that rotates, so the per-(ip,email) counter never reaches 5 from any single key.
